s: to be present together or with
6101.lxx: in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 *
6101.full: συν-πάρειμι (Rec. σνμπ-), [in LXX: Tob.12:12 ΑΒ, Pro.8:27 (?), Wis.9:10 * ;] to be present together or with: with dative of person(s), Act.25:24.† (AS)

6103.lxx: in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15,  TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A *
6103.full: συμφωνία, -ας, ἡ (σύμφωνος), [in LXX: Dan LXX TH Dan.3:5, 15, TH Dan.3:7, 10 (סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה) 4Ma.14:3 A * ;] __1. symphony, music: Luk.15:25 __2. a musical instrument (Polyb., al.; Da, ll. with; v MM, xxiv).† (AS)

6104.full: συν-ακολουθέω, -ῶ [in LXX: 2Ma.2:4 2Mac 2:6 * ;] to follow along with, accompany: with dative of person(s), Mrk.14:51, Luk.23:49; before μετά, with genitive of person(s), Mrk.5:37.† (AS)

6105.full: συν-αυξάνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:4, 4Ma.13:27 * ;] to cause to increase or grow together. Pass., to grow together: Mat.13:30 (Xen., al.).† (AS)

s: the members of a picnic party
6106.full: to dine or sup with another, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus); μετά τινων (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to dine or sup with others , (Xenophon Historicus), etc.; οἱ ξυνδειπνοῦντες the members of a picnic party , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

6108.full: συνδρομή, -ῆς, ἡ (συντρέχω), [in LXX: Jdth.10:18, 3Ma.3:8 * ;] concourse, esp. of a riotous gathering: Act.21:30 (Arist., Polyb., al.).† (AS)

6109.lxx: in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 *
6109.full: συν-εγείρω [in LXX: Exo.23:5 B2 (עָזַב), Isa.14:9 (עוּר pil.), 4Ma.2:14 * ;] to raise together: metaphorically, of the Christian's mystical resur­rection with Christ, Eph.2:6; pass., Col.2:12 3:1.† (AS)

6111.full: συν-ελαύνω [in LXX: 2Ma.4:26 2Mac 4:42 2Mac 5:5 * ;] to drive together, force together: εἰς εἰρήνην, Act.7:26, Rec. (WH, RV, συνήλλασσεν).† (AS)

s: In Hellenistic writers , trans., to cause to work together
6115.full: συνεργέω, -ῶ [in LXX: I Est.7:2, 1Ma.12:1 * ;] __1. prop., to work together (with): absol., Mrk.16:20, 1Co.16:16, 2Co.6:1; with dative, Jas.2:22; dative commod., Rom.8:28, T, R, txt. (but see infr.). __2. In Hellenistic writers (M, Pr., 65), trans., to cause to work together (cf. ICC, in l): with accusative of thing(s), Rom.8:28 [WH] R, mg. (but see supr.).† (AS)

6116.full: συνεργός, -όν [in LXX: 2Ma.8:7 Mac 14:5 * ;] a fellow-worker: with genitive of person(s), Rom.16:3, 9 16:21, Php.2:25 4:3, 1Th.3:2, Rec., Phm 1 24; θεοῦ (cf. Lft., Notes, 41, 188), 1Co.3:9 (pl.), 1Th.3:2 [WH] R, mg. (R, txt., διάκονον τοῦ θ.; on the original reading, see ICC, in l); τ. χαρᾶς ὑηῶν, 2Co.1:24; τ. ἀληθείᾳ, III Jn 8; before εἰς, 2Co.8:23, Col.4:11.† (AS)

s: In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience
6118.lxx: in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א *
6118.full: συν-είδησις, -εως, ἡ (συνεῖδον), [in LXX: Ecc.10:20 (מַדָּע), Wis.17:11, Sir.42:18 א * ;] __1. consciousness: with genitive obj., Heb.10:2, 1Pe.2:19. __2. In ethical sense, innate discernment, self-judging consciousness, conscience (Stoics and late writers): Rom.2:15 9:1, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.1:12 4:2 5:11, 1Ti.4:2, Heb.9:14; σ. ἀγαθή, Act.23:1, 1Ti.1:5 1:19, 1Pe.3:16 3:21; ἀσθενής, 1Co.8:7 8:10; ἀσθενοῦσα, 1Co.8:12; ἀπρόσκοπος, Act.24:16; καθαρά, 1Ti.3:9, 2Ti.1:3; καλή, Heb.13:18; πονηρά, Heb.10:22; ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ σ., Tit.1:15; διὰ τὴν σ., Rom.13:5, 1Co.10:25 10:27-28; κατὰ σ., Heb.9:9; ὑπὸ (τῆς) σ., Jhn.8:1-59 [9] (Rec.), 1Co.10:29 (cf. Cremer, 233 ff.; ICC on Rom.2:15; DB, i, 468 ff.).† (AS)

6121.full: a mutual agreement, covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: in plural dealings between men , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

6122.full: to sew or stitch together, sew up , Lat. consuo, (Hesiod) (ML)

6125.full: to be gangrened , ἐσφακέλισε τὸ ὀστέον (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to throw as from a sling
to move like a swing, to swing to and fro
6126.full: 1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) from σφενδόνη (ML)

6127.full: σφυρόν, -οῦ, τό, [in LXX: Job.41:21 (לָהַט) * ;] the ankle: Act.3:7, Rec. (T, WH, σφυδρόν; see Bl., § 6, 8).† (AS)

6128.full: a wedge , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.;—;used as an instrument of torture , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

6129.full: 1. a vertebra , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in plural the backbone, spine , or the neck , (Euripides) 2. Lat. verticillus, the round weight attached to a spindle, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: of or for the body, bodily
6131.full: σωματικός, -ή, -όν (σῶμα), [in LXX: 4Ma.1:32 4Mac 3:1 * ;] __(a) of or for the body, bodily: γυμνασία, 1Ti.4:8; __(b) (opposite to ἀσώματος) bodily, corporeal: εἶδος, Luk.3:22.† (AS)

6132.full: σωρεύω [in LXX: Pro.25:22 (חָתָה), Jdth.15:11 * ;] __(a) to heap on: with accusative before ἐπί with accusative, Rom.12:20 (LXX) (Arist., al.); __(b) to heap with: with accusative and dative, metaphorically, ἁμαρτίαις, 2Ti.3:6 (overwhelmed with, Field, Notes, 217) (Polyb.).† (AS)

6134.full: σάτον, -ου, τό (Aram. סָאתָא = Heb. סְאָה), [in LXX: Hag.2:17 (16)* ;] a Hebrew measure (= about a peck and a half): Mat.13:33, Luk.13:21.† (AS)

6135.full: 1. Pass. to lie together , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. as Pass. of συντίθημι, to be composed or compounded , ἔκ τινων of certain parts, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. of written works, to be composed , (Thucydides), etc. 4. to be contrived, concocted , (Euripides), etc. 5. to be agreed on by two parties, (Thucydides): in participle agreed on, arranged , αἱ συγκείμεναι ἡμέραι (Herdotus Historicus); κατὰ τὰ συγκείμενα according to the terms agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν ξυγκειμένων (Thucydides) 6. impersonal σύγκειται, it has been or is agreed on , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; so, συγκειμένου σφι, with infinitive, since they had agreed to . . , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine
6138.full: 1. that which is put together in order : 2. a body of troops, squadron, contingent , (Xenophon Historicus) 3. the constitution of a state , ς. πολιτείας a form of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 4. an arrangement of musical notes , (Aristotle Philosopher) 5. a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine , (Plutarch) 6. = σύνταξις II. 3, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

s: a meeting, a knot of men
6139.full: 1. a putting together, composition , (Aristotle Philosopher); ς. προσώπου a studied expression of countenance, of Pericles, (Plutarch) 2. a bringing together, introduction, recommendation , (Polybius Historicus) 3. συνίσταμαι); a standing together, meeting : in hostile sense, close combat, conflict , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, ς. γνώμης a conflict of mind, intense anxiety, (Thucydides) 4. a meeting, a knot of men , (Euripides); κατὰ ξυστάσεις γιγνόμενοι forming into knots , (Thucydides): a political union , (Demosthenes Orator) 5. friendship or alliance , (Polybius Historicus): a conspiracy , (Plutarch) 6. construction, structure, constitution , (Plato Philosophus): absolute a political constitution , (Plato Philosophus) 7. metaphorically of the mind, ς. φρενῶν contraction, sternness, sullenness , (Euripides) (ML)

6141.full: 1. to be controller of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive, τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed or possessed by one, (Pindar) 5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

6142.full: 1. troublous, turbulent , (Herdotus Historicus); ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. troubled, disordered , (Aristotle Philosopher) 3. of an army, (Thucydides) 4. adverb, ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion , (Isocrates Orator); τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously disposed, (Demosthenes Orator); Sup. -έστατα (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

6144.full: 1. a broad strap for bearing anything from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 2. a leathern strap or belt , for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 3. a broad linen bandage for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6148.full: 1. delightsome, delightful, pleasant, agreeable, glad , (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; τὸ τερπνόν delight, pleasure , (Thucydides); τὰ τερπνά delights, pleasures , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. of persons, αὑτῷ τερπνός with joy to himself, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;comparative and Sup. τερπνότερος, -ότατος, (Theognis Elegiacus); later, -ιστος:—;adverb τερπνῶς, (Theognis Elegiacus) (ML)

s: so great, so noble, so bad
6151.full: antecedent to οἷος, as ἀοιδοῦ τοιοῦδ᾽ οἷος ὅδ᾽ ἐστί of such a minstrel as is this one, (Odyssey by Homer); absolute, ἀλλ᾽ ὅδ᾽ ἐγὼ τοιόσδε here am I such as you see , (Odyssey by Homer):—;also, so great, so noble, so bad , τοιάδε λαίφη such clothes, i. e. so bad , (Odyssey by Homer); τοσόσδε καὶ τοιόσδε (Herdotus Historicus):—;also with a qualifying word, τοιόσδ᾽ ἠμὲν δέμας ἠδὲ καὶ ἔργα such both in form and works, (Odyssey by Homer):—;with the Art., ὁ τ. ἀνήρ (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; οἱ τοιοίδε (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐν τῷ τοιῷδε in such circumstances, (Herdotus Historicus):—;the sense is made more indefinite in τοιόσδε τις such a one, (Thucydides):—;neuter plural τοιάδε as follows , τοιαῦτα as aforesaid , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to the place from which it was cut
6152.full: 1. the end left after cutting, the stump of a tree, (Iliad by Homer); δοκοῦ τ. the end of a beam, (Thucydides); λίθοι ἐν τομῇ ἐγγώνιοι stones cut square, (Thucydides); so, τομῇ προσθεῖσα βόστρυχον having fitted the lock to the place from which it was cut , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. a cutting, hewing, cleaving , ἐν τομᾷ σιδήρου by stroke of iron, (Sophocles Tragicus); φασγάνου τομαί (Euripides):—;as a surgical operation, τομῇ χρῆσθαι (Plato Philosophus); διὰ καύσεών τε καὶ τομῶν by cautery and the knife , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6156.full: 1. on the third day , used with Verbs so as to agree with the subject, τριταῖοι ἐγένοντο ἐν τῇ Ἀττικῇ (Herdotus Historicus); ἐσβεβληκὼς τριταῖος ἐς Μηλιέας having invaded Melis three days before , (Herdotus Historicus); τρ. γενόμενος after being three days dead, (Herdotus Historicus):—; τριταῖος (i.e. πυρετός); a tertian fever , (Plato Philosophus) 2. of events, lasting three days , (Euripides) 3. generally for τρίτος, (Euripides) (ML)

6161.full: τρίχινος, -η, -ον (θρίξ), [in LXX: Zec.13:4 (שֵׂעָר), Exo.26:7 * ;] of hair: στόκος, Rev.6:12 (Xen., Plat., al.).† (AS)

6166.full: τάχα (ταχύς), adv., [in LXX: Wis.13:6 14:19 * ;] __(a) (chiefly poët.), quickly, presently; __(b) perhaps: Rom.5:7, Phm 15.† (AS)

6167.lxx: in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi.
6167.full: τάχειον, see: ταχύ. ταχύ (neut. of ταχύς), adv., [in LXX chiefly for מָהַר pi. ;] quickly, speedily, forthwith: Mat.5:25 28:7-8, Mrk.9:39, Luk.15:22, Jhn.11:29, Rev.2:16 3:11 11:14 22:7, 12 22:2 o. Compar., τάχειον (T, Rec. τάχιον), = cl. θᾶσσον, θᾶττον (Att..), (see Bl., § 44, 3): Jhn.13:27 20:4, 1Ti.3:14 (T, Rec.), Heb.13:19, 23 Superl., τάχιστα: ὡς τ., as quickly as possible (BL, § 11, 3), Act.17:15.† (AS)

6169.lxx: in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) *
6169.full: τίλλω [in LXX: Est.9:3, Isa.18:7, Dan LXX 7:4 (מָרַט) * ;] to pluck, pluck off: στάχυας, Mat.12:1, Mrk.2:23, Luk.6:1.† (AS)

6170.full: φαντάζω (φαίνω) [in LXX: Wis.6:16, Sir.31:5 (34:5)* ;] to make visible. In cl. used in pass. only, = φαίνομαι, to become visible, appear: ptcp., Heb.12:21.† (AS)

6172.full: 1. a sparing , νεκύων (Iliad by Homer) 2. absolute thrift, parsimony , (Odyssey by Homer): thrift in exposing oneself to danger, (Thucydides) (ML)

6174.full: 1. the sound of the voice, a voice , (Pindar), etc.: of a person, ὦ φθέγμ᾽ ἀναιδές, for ὦ φθεγξάμενε ἀναιδῆ, (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. language, speech , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a saying, word , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. of other sounds, as of birds, cries , (Sophocles Tragicus); of a bull, roaring , (Euripides); φθ. θυείας the grinding of the mortar, (Aristophanes Comicus); of the nightingale's song, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

6175.full: φθόγγος, -ου, ὁ (φθέγγομαι), [in LXX: Psa.19:4 (קַו), Wis.19:18 * ;] a sound: Rom.10:18 (LXX) 1Co.14:7.† (AS)

6179.full: φιλόστοργος, -ον (στοργή, family affection), [in LXX: 4Ma.15:13 * ;] tenderly loving, affectionate (Xen., Plut., al.): of Christians, Rom.12:10.† (AS)

6180.full: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

6184.lxx: in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc.
6184.full: φράσσω [in LXX: Job.38:8 (סָכַךְ hi.), Hos.2:6(8) (שׂוּךְ), Pro.21:13 (אָטַם), etc. ;] to fence in, stop, close: στόματα λεόντων, Heb.11:33; στόμα, metaphorically, Rom.3:19; pass., καύχησις, 2Co.11:10.† (AS)

6185.full: 1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6186.full: φρόνημα, -τος, τό (φρονέω), [in LXX: 2Ma.7:21 2Mac 13:9 * ;] that which is in the mind (the content of φρονεῖν, ICC, Ro., 88), the thought: Rom.8:6-7, 27.† (AS)

6187.full: 1. to roast or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted barley, (Thucydides) 2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

6189.full: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

6190.full: 1. transitive to puff or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. metaphorically to puff one up, make him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 3. to blow up, kindle a fire: but also 4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 6. to blow a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

6191.full: φωτεινός (WH, φωτινός), ή, όν (φῶς), [in LXX: Sir.17:31 23:19 * ;] bright, light: νεφέλη, Mat.17:5; opposite to σκοτεινός, Mat.6:22, Luk.11:34, 36.† (AS)

6192.full: φίλημα, -τος, τό (φιλέω), [in LXX: Pro.27:6, Sng.1:2 (נְשִׁיקָה) * ;] a kiss: Luk.7:45 22:48; as a token of Christian brotherhood, φ. ἅγιον, Rom.16:16, 1Co.16:20, 2Co.13:12, 1Th.5:26; φ. ἀγάπης, 1Pe.5:14 (see Lft., Notes, 90; DB, DCA, see word "Kiss").† (AS)

6198.full: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

6199.full: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)
